title: Essentials bar throws a Lua error and never appears in a raid with about eight or more providers
clients: All clients (Retail and MoP raids and battlegrounds hit it most; Era, TBC and Forever need nine or more druids, or shamans plus druids on TBC)
what: In a raid or battleground where the Bloodlust and Battle Rez headers plus their providers fill the bar's 10 rows, every refresh stops with a Lua error before the bar is shown, so the Essentials bar never appears. The same error cuts short the roster scan, so the Lane view also doesn't open on joining, and /cdc roster prints nothing. It fires on every roster change, cast, level-up and flask/food message.
proof: Essentials.lua:149 and :164 increment idx then 'if idx > MAX_ROWS then break end' (MAX_ROWS = 10, :11), so idx is left at 11 when the list overflows; the flask strip also does 'idx = idx + 1' at :207 even when it then skips drawing ('if idx <= MAX_ROWS'). The layout pass then walks past the pool: ':226 for i = 1, idx do  :227 local row = rows[i]  :228 row:ClearAllPoints()' -> rows[11] is nil -> 'attempt to index a nil value (local row)'. The Show at :234-235 is after it, so the bar stays hidden. Roster.lua:136-138: 'if CC.RefreshEssentials then CC:RefreshEssentials() end' runs before 'if CC.RefreshLanes then CC:RefreshLanes() end', so the lane refresh is skipped too; CooldownCollaborator.lua:395-396 has the same order in RefreshAllViews. /cdc roster calls ScanRoster (CooldownCollaborator.lua:663) before printing. Probe (tools/tests/run.js with a 12-member raid: 3 DK, 2 druid, 2 shaman, 2 mage, 1 evoker) on Mainline, Vanilla (10 druids) and Camelot (10 druids): GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE -> './Essentials.lua:228: attempt to index a nil value (local 'row')', essentialsFrame:IsShown() false. Threshold: headers + providers >= 10 (the flask strip makes it 11); the suite's 3-member party never reaches it.

title: Main panel in a raid fills with READY rows and stops showing any running timers
what: Every tracked spell anyone has used stays on the panel as READY for the rest of the session, and READY rows are sorted to the top of a 14-row list. In a raid, after a few pulls there are more than 14 READY rows, so the panel shows only READY and none of the cooldowns that are actually running. Flask and food buffs are recorded and shared as one- or two-hour 'cooldowns' too (they can't be unticked), and turn into permanent READY rows once that time passes, which fills the list faster. Nothing says rows are hidden.
proof: State is never cleared for players still in the group (only PruneState drops leavers, Events.lua:102-112), and a ready-now just re-dates the entry (CooldownCollaborator.lua:281 'entry.spells[spellID] = GetTime() - data.duration'). UI.lua:164 keeps ready rows by default ('if remaining > 0 or self.db.showReady', showReady = true at CooldownCollaborator.lua:134). UI.lua:179-181 sorts them first: 'if a.remaining == 0 and b.remaining > 0 then return true end', then :191 'local count = math.min(#rowData, MAX_ROWS)' with MAX_ROWS = 14 (:4). Consumables: Consumables.lua:185 'CC:RecordCooldown("player", id)' on each flask/food rising edge -> CooldownCollaborator.lua:270 SendCooldownSync, receivers keep them (built-ins are in their SpellData, CooldownCollaborator.lua:170-172), BuildRowData has no consumable filter (UI.lua:159-161), and the Default Spells list skips them so they can't be unticked (Options.lua:64 'if not data.custom and not data.consumable'). Probe: 10 ready Rebirths + 6 ready Tranquilities + 1 Innervate on cooldown -> 17 rows, no running timer among the 14 shown (Mainline, Vanilla, Camelot).

title: Flask/food status is only sent when your buffs change, so late joiners and anyone who reloads see everyone as missing
what: Your flask and food status goes out once (the first check after login) and then only when one of your buffs appears or drops. If you log in solo and then join a group with a flask on, the group never hears about it. Anyone who joins later, or does a /reload mid-raid, sees every already-buffed player as missing a flask and food until that player's buffs next change. A status change during a Retail encounter, when addon messages are blocked, is dropped and never retried.
proof: Consumables.lua:223-225: 'if changed or not self.buffBroadcastDone then self.buffBroadcastDone = true self:BroadcastBuffStatus(...)'. BroadcastBuffStatus returns early when solo (:239 'if not IsInGroup() then return end') but buffBroadcastDone is already true. Nothing else sends CDCBUFF: no GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE hook, no request message, and BroadcastState (Events.lua:116-126) only resends cooldowns. The send result is ignored (:245 'C_ChatInfo.SendAddonMessage(BUFF_PREFIX, msg, chatType)'), unlike SendCooldownSync's retry queue. Receivers fill buffRoster only from messages (:252); a reload starts it empty (:24). Probe on Mainline, Mists and Camelot: flask on while solo, then join a party and run 6 s of polls -> 0 CDCBUFF messages sent.

title: Flask/food strip counts you twice in a raid (shows 21 people in a 20-player raid)
what: In a raid the 'Flask N/N  Food N/N' line counts you twice: the total is one higher than the raid size, and your own flask and food count twice. Totals are always wrong in raids, and the colour can be green or red for the wrong reason.
proof: Consumables.lua:284-286: 'check("player")' then 'if IsInRaid() then for i = 1, GetNumGroupMembers() do check("raid" .. i) end'. In a raid, raid1..raidN includes the player, and check() adds to total and hasFlask/hasFood with no de-duplication by name (:267-281). The party branch correctly uses GetNumGroupMembers() - 1. Probe: 12-member raid (player is one of the raid tokens) -> GetGroupBuffStatus().total = 13 on Mainline, Vanilla and Camelot.

title: Unticking a spell, or raising the minimum cooldown, stops you telling your group about that spell
clients: Retail, Forever (Era, TBC and MoP partly cover it from the combat log, within its range)
what: Unticking a spell under Default Spells, or picking a higher 'Minimum cooldown to track', is meant to tidy your own panel, but it also stops your own casts of those spells from being sent. Groupmates see that spell as READY while it's on cooldown, CooldownTimeline3 doesn't get it, and no ready-now goes out. For example, a druid who unticks Rebirth still shows as READY on everyone's Essentials bar after using it, and the leader's Rez button can pick them.
proof: CooldownCollaborator.lua:250-251 return before anything is recorded or sent: 'if data.duration < (self.db.minDuration or 60) then return end' and 'if self.db.disabledSpells and self.db.disabledSpells[spellID] then return end'; SendCooldownSync (:270), BridgeStart (:271) and the localActive watch (:266-268) come after. The display already filters both at render time (UI.lua:160-161), so the early return isn't needed for the panel. Other players' Essentials/Request Rez rely on comm data on Retail and Forever (Roster.lua:263-266 GetRemaining for non-local entries). Probe (Mainline): disabledSpells[29166] = true, own UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED 29166 -> 0 CDCOLLAB messages.

title: Main panel opens itself again after you close it while in a group
what: In a group, closing the main panel with /cdc or a left-click on the minimap button only lasts until the next cast, sync message or roster change, which happens constantly in a raid. There's no close button and no setting to keep it hidden, so a player who only wants the Essentials bar or Lane view can't get rid of it in a group.
proof: UI.lua:222-225 at the end of every RefreshRows: '-- Auto-show when in a group with data / if IsInGroup() then self.frame:Show() end' (it shows even without data). RefreshRows runs from RefreshAllViews on every recorded/synced cast (CooldownCollaborator.lua:272, :283, :307, :394) and on every GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE (:578). The toggles only flip visibility: CooldownCollaborator.lua:692-693 'CC.frame:SetShown(not CC.frame:IsShown())', Minimap.lua:63-65 the same. Probe (Mainline): in a party, /cdc -> shown false; a party member's synced cast -> shown true; hide again then GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE -> shown true.

title: With panel scale set to anything but 1.0, the main panel shifts toward a screen corner on every reload
what: Set 'Panel scale' to, say, 1.5 and the panel moves on every /reload or login: down and left at scales above 1.0, up and right below 1.0, until it sits clamped in a corner. Clicking a locked panel also saves the shifted spot. The position saved with the panel doesn't survive a scale other than 1.0.
proof: SavePosition mixes coordinate spaces: UI.lua:236-240 'local x, y = self.frame:GetCenter()' (frame's own scaled units) minus 'UIParent:GetCenter()' (UIParent units). BuildUI restores it as a frame-space offset: UI.lua:34-35 'frame:SetPoint("CENTER", UIParent, "CENTER", db.x, db.y)' then 'frame:SetScale(db.scale)'. With scale s and UIParent centre U: on screen the panel sits at U + db.x*s, and GetCenter returns (U + db.x*s)/s, so saving gives db.x' = db.x + U(1/s - 1), which moves the panel U(1 - s) per session (about 340 x 190 UI units per reload at s = 1.5). SavePosition runs at every PLAYER_LOGOUT (CooldownCollaborator.lua:614-615) and every mouse-up even when locked (UI.lua:55-58). Scale is user-set (Options.lua:376-380 'CC.db.scale = v ... CC.frame:SetScale(v)'). The stub's GetCenter returns 0,0, so this is from the code, not a probe; a frame the player has dragged may also get restored by the client's own layout cache, which can hide the shift.

title: /cdc lock doesn't lock the Essentials bar or Lane view, and nothing else can
what: '/cdc lock' and the 'Lock panel position' box lock only the main panel. The Essentials bar and Lane view always drag on a left-click, so a stray click mid-fight moves them, and no command or setting locks them. The addon still prints 'CooldownCollaborator locked.'
proof: CooldownCollaborator.lua:622-625 sets only 'CC.db.locked = true' then CC:UpdateLock() (UI.lua:228-231, main frame only); Options.lua:259-260 the same. essentialsLocked / laneLocked are declared (CooldownCollaborator.lua:146, :152) and read (Essentials.lua:48 'not CC.db.essentialsLocked', Lanes.lua:25 'not CC.db.laneLocked') but no code anywhere sets them (grep: only the defaults and these reads). Probe: after /cdc lock -> locked true, essentialsLocked false, laneLocked false.

title: Lane view drops the READY providers first once a lane has more than six
what: Each lane draws only six icons and keeps the six with the longest time left, so the providers who are ready, the ones that matter, are cut first. With seven or more Battle Rez or lust providers on cooldown, the lane shows nobody ready even when someone is.
proof: Lanes.lua:59 'for i = 1, 6 do' builds six icons per lane; :100 'table.sort(status, function(a, b) return a.remaining > b.remaining end)' puts ready entries (remaining 0) last; :109-110 'for i, icon in ipairs(lane.icons) do local entry = status[i]' shows only status[1..6]. Probe (Mainline, Mists, Camelot): 8 druids in a raid, 7 with Rebirth on cooldown, 1 ready -> ready among the six lane icons = 0.

title: Lane view: ready icons pile straight down, out of the frame and over the next lane
what: Ready providers all sit at the same spot on the right end of the lane, so each one is pushed one row lower. At the start of every raid everyone is ready, so with three or more providers the icons run off the bottom of the Lane view and over the Battle Rez lane, or hang below the window.
proof: Lanes.lua:117 'local progress = entry.ready and 1 or ...' -> identical xPos for every ready entry (:120). The bin-pack at :122-136 finds every slot taken ('math.abs(ox - xPos) < ICON_SIZE') and raises level each time; :139 'local yOffset = -level * (ICON_SIZE - 4)', with no cap and no wrap. Frame height is fixed at 'LANE_HEIGHT * laneCount + LANE_GAP * (laneCount - 1) + 30' (:19) = 92 on Retail/MoP/TBC, 58 on Era/Forever. Probe: 6 ready druids -> lowest icon offset -90 from the Battle Rez lane centre, which is itself 70 (Retail) / 36 (Forever) below the frame top: about 68 px below the frame's bottom edge.

title: Lane view icons are covered by a solid coloured square instead of a border
what: The 'border' meant to frame each lane icon is a filled square, 60% opaque, drawn on top of the icon. Ready icons look like green blobs and cooling ones like class-coloured blobs, with the spell icon only faintly visible.
proof: Lanes.lua:60 icon on the 'ARTWORK' layer; :65-66 'local border = lane:CreateTexture(nil, "OVERLAY")' sized ICON_SIZE + 4 and centred on the icon (:148-149); :150 'icon.border:SetColorTexture(c[1], c[2], c[3], 0.6)' fills the whole 26x26 texture. OVERLAY draws above ARTWORK, so the fill covers the 22x22 icon.

title: Removing a custom spell that has a built-in spell's ID deletes the built-in spell until /reload
what: The Custom Spells tab is the obvious way to give a built-in spell a different cooldown (for example a talented Innervate or Rebirth). Adding it replaces the built-in entry: it disappears from Default Spells and loses its class. Pressing Remove then deletes the spell entirely, so your casts and your group's stop being tracked or sent until you reload, and a provider spell like Rebirth loses its Essentials icon.
proof: CooldownCollaborator.lua:218-224 AddCustomSpell overwrites 'CC.SpellData[spellID] = { ..., class = "UNKNOWN", custom = true }' with no check for an existing built-in (ranks and level are lost too). RemoveCustomSpell :233-235: 'if CC.SpellData[spellID] and CC.SpellData[spellID].custom then CC.SpellData[spellID] = nil end', and the built-in is never restored (it comes back only at Init). With no data, RecordCooldown returns at :249, RecordCooldownFromComm at :295, Essentials skips the icon (Essentials.lua:174). Default Spells hides custom entries (Options.lua:64). Probe (all three clients): Rebirth class DRUID -> after AddCustomSpell(20484, 300) UNKNOWN -> after RemoveCustomSpell(20484) SpellData[20484] = nil.

title: Rez button posts to party or raid chat in Dungeon Finder, LFR and battleground groups, where those channels don't reach the group
clients: Retail, MoP Classic (clients with instance groups)
what: In a Dungeon Finder party, Raid Finder or a battleground, the leader's Rez request goes to /party or /raid. Those are home-group channels, so the game rejects the line and the druid or death knight never sees it (in a raid only the raid warning may get through). The addon's own sync already switches to instance chat in these groups; the Rez request doesn't.
proof: CooldownCollaborator.lua:385-390: 'if IsInRaid() then SendChat(msg, "RAID") SendChat(msg, "RAID_WARNING") else SendChat(msg, "PARTY") end'. Comms.lua:18-20 picks 'INSTANCE_CHAT' when 'IsInGroup(LE_PARTY_CATEGORY_INSTANCE)' (commit 41c65fc 'INSTANCE_CHAT in instance groups'), but RequestRez doesn't use CC:GroupChannel(). Probe (Mainline, INSTANCE_GROUP = true, party): chat goes to [PARTY] while CC:GroupChannel() = INSTANCE_CHAT. That the server rejects PARTY/RAID in an instance-only group is client behaviour, not shown in the stub.

title: Essentials bar lists offline druids and death knights as READY, and the Rez button can call on them
what: A raid member who has disconnected still shows on the Essentials bar as a READY Battle Rez or lust provider. When the leader presses Rez, the addon can name that offline player in raid warning ('Bob, please Rebirth Ann!'), and the rez never comes.
proof: Roster.lua:104-115 addUnit keeps any unit with a name and class; there's no UnitIsConnected check (offline members still return both). GetCapabilityStatus (:240-283) lists every roster entry with no connection test, and a provider with no observed cast is 'ready = (bestRemaining or 0) <= 0' (:281). RequestRez skips only the dead (CooldownCollaborator.lua:367-369 'if not token or not UnitIsDeadOrGhost(token) then provider = entry'); an offline unit isn't dead or ghost. Only the flask strip filters offline players (Consumables.lua:269).

title: Rez button accepts a dead monster or a stranger as the target
what: If the leader still has the dead boss or a dead mob targeted (or a dead player from outside the group) and presses Rez, the addon posts '<druid>, please Rebirth <mob>!' to raid chat and raid warning. It only checks that the target is dead, not that it's a player in your group.
proof: CooldownCollaborator.lua:356 'if not UnitExists("target") or not UnitIsDeadOrGhost("target") then' is the only target check (no UnitIsPlayer / UnitInRaid / UnitInParty, grep finds none). :361 'local targetName = self:FullName("target")' works for NPCs (realm falls back to ours, :88). Probe (Mainline): dead target 'Hogger' -> chat '[PARTY] Tania, please Rebirth Hogger!'.

title: Flask and food timers restart at full length on every login and /reload, for you and your whole group
what: A flask or food buff is timed from when the addon first sees it, not from when you used it. After a /reload or login, a flask with ten minutes left shows its full hour (or two hours on Classic) again, and that restarted time is sent to everyone, overwriting the timer on their panels and on CooldownTimeline3. Re-drinking a flask before it runs out doesn't restart it, so it counts down to READY while the flask is still up.
proof: Consumables.lua:182-187: 'local wasActive = self.consumableActive[id]; if present and not wasActive then CC:RecordCooldown("player", id) end'. consumableActive starts empty each session (:23). RecordCooldown stamps 'now' (CooldownCollaborator.lua:260-261) and sends secondsAgo 0 (:270). Receivers take it as a newer cast (:303-305 'if not cur or usedAt > cur'). A buff kept up continuously never re-records because present stays true. On Era/TBC/MoP the aura's real expiration is readable (ScanPlayerBuffs reads the aura table, :136) but isn't used.

title: A /cdc consumable entry can never be removed
what: Once you register a buff with /cdc consumable, there's no command or settings control to remove it, and the settings window doesn't list consumables at all. A wrong spell ID (say, a common raid buff) stays tracked for good: it keeps being sent to the group as a cooldown whenever it lands on you.
proof: CC:RemoveConsumableBuff is defined at Consumables.lua:108-117 but never called (grep 'RemoveConsumableBuff': only the definition). The slash handler has only the add path (CooldownCollaborator.lua:651-661). Options.lua lists customSpells only (:152), never consumableBuffs. Entries reload every session (Consumables.lua:51-62) and are polled every 2 s (:197-219, :295).

title: A flask added the way /cdc consumable's help line shows never counts toward 'Flask N/N'
what: The usage line the addon prints and the README both say '/cdc consumable <spellID> <seconds> <name>'. An entry only counts toward the Flask or Food total if the name ends in a separate lowercase word 'flask' or 'food', which isn't mentioned there. So '/cdc consumable 1230876 3600 Flask' or '... Haste Flask' is tracked but never counted.
proof: CooldownCollaborator.lua:658 prints 'usage: /cdc consumable <spellID> <durationSeconds> <name>'; README.md:81 the same. Consumables.lua:77-79: 'name:match("^(.-)%s+(flask)$")' / '(food)$': case-sensitive, and the keyword needs a word before it, so a name that is just 'Flask' or ends 'Flask' sets no category. GetGroupBuffStatus counts only 'cat == "flask"' / '"food"' (:213-216). Data_Retail.lua:71-72 says the real Midnight flask IDs still have to be found and registered by hand, so Retail players are the ones most likely to use this command.

title: Settings window's 'Lock panel position' tick goes stale after /cdc lock or /cdc unlock
what: The settings window is built once and reused. If you open it, close it, then type /cdc unlock, reopening it still shows the panel as locked. Clicking the box then does the opposite of what it shows.
proof: Options.lua:258 'cbLock:SetChecked(CC.db.locked)' runs only when the window is first built; later opens just toggle visibility (:191-193 'self.optionsFrame:SetShown(...) return'). /cdc lock / unlock change CC.db.locked (CooldownCollaborator.lua:622-629) without touching the checkbox. The box's OnClick saves 'widget:GetChecked()' (:260), the flipped stale value.

title: 'No custom spells added yet.' stays on screen under the first custom spell you add
what: On the Custom Spells tab, the 'No custom spells added yet.' message stays after you add a spell and sits under the new row's icon and name. Each empty refresh adds another copy.
proof: RefreshSpellList clears only child frames: Options.lua:146 'for _, c in pairs({ content:GetChildren() }) do c:Hide(); c:SetParent(nil) end'. The message is a FontString region on content (:181-183 'content:CreateFontString(...)' at TOPLEFT 0,0, where the first row also sits, :157), and regions are never hidden here (RefreshDefaultSpellList does hide them, :60). Probe: label made and shown while empty; after AddCustomSpell + RefreshSpellList it is still shown.

title: Custom Spells: 'Shift-click a spell link to auto-fill' doesn't work
what: The Custom Spells tab tells you to shift-click a spell link to fill the box. Nothing routes a shift-clicked link into that box, so the click goes to chat (if it's open) or does nothing, and the box stays empty.
proof: Options.lua:444 hint text 'Shift-click a spell link to auto-fill (spellbook must be open).' The only link handling is OnTextChanged (:480-490), which reacts to text already in the box. No hook on ChatEdit_InsertLink / ChatFrameUtil.InsertLink or HandleModifiedItemClick exists (grep finds none). Blizzard's link insert targets the active chat edit box and a few named Blizzard boxes, not an arbitrary focused addon EditBox. That last point is client behaviour, not shown in the stub.

title: On a fresh install the Essentials bar sits on top of the main panel
what: The default spots put the Essentials bar's left edge 50 pixels into the right side of the main panel, at the same height. Both open on their own the first time you join a group, so new players see them overlapping until they drag one away.
proof: Main panel: 320 wide (UI.lua:3) centred at x = 0, y = 200 (CooldownCollaborator.lua:129-130), spanning x -160..160. Essentials: 220 wide (Essentials.lua:10) centred at x = 220, y = 200 (CooldownCollaborator.lua:143-144), spanning x 110..330, so they overlap from x 110 to 160 at the same height. Both are MEDIUM strata (UI.lua:37, Essentials.lua:24), both auto-show in a group (UI.lua:223-225, Essentials.lua:234-235), and essentialsEnabled defaults to true (:142).

title: Dragging the minimap button goes wrong when the minimap is scaled (Edit Mode minimap size)
clients: Retail (any client where the minimap's scale differs from the UI's)
what: With the minimap set larger or smaller than 100% in Edit Mode, dragging the button around the minimap doesn't follow the cursor: it jumps to the wrong side or sticks to one arc. The angle is worked out against a minimap centre measured in a different scale from the cursor.
proof: Minimap.lua:72-75: 'local mx, my = Minimap:GetCenter()' (Minimap's own scaled units) with 'local s = UIParent:GetEffectiveScale()' and 'math.atan2(py / s - my, px / s - mx)'. The cursor is divided by UIParent's scale, not the Minimap's (LibDBIcon uses Minimap:GetEffectiveScale()). When the minimap cluster has its own scale, the two points are in different units and the angle is skewed. That Edit Mode's minimap Size works through SetScale is client behaviour, not shown in the stub.
